. Like other event maps, this map had a specialized wave structure with special enemies. Players started with a varying amount of cash, based on how many players there were in a match. The rewards you received were based on how many waves you survive and if you won the match. This map had two difficulties, Easy and Hard.

Cash was only gained if an enemy was killed, or in some cases, damaged by a specific amount of health. Additionally, the amount gained was a set amount of cash, which was not always equal to the enemy's health. In solo, you received 100% of the cash when an enemy was killed, or if it was damaged enough. With each additional player, this decreased by 25%, which meant that in a quad, you only got 25% of the cash. This amount was distributed between players based on how much damage they dealt. However, if a player did not deal any damage, they would receive a percentage of the enemy's full cash upon its death or when it was damaged enough, which was 12.5% in duo, 16.7% in trio and 18.75% in quad. If it was a decimal, it got rounded up or down depending on the decimal value. If it was at least 0.5, it got rounded up. If it was less than 0.5, it got rounded down. For example, the
in quad between the players that damaged it. Players that did not damage it received

Health of enemies in this mode scaled with player count, starting at three players. The health increase was 10% in duo, 20% in trio, 30% in Easy quad and 50% in Hard quad, with an added set amount of health added on top of that increase. It was applied after attributes, like

, meaning they could affect the health of an enemy differently. The first increase was not always the stated percentage, while the second increase had a varied amount it increased health by, both affected by enemy health.
This map featured one boss, the
, which appeared at Wave 25 on Easy difficulty and Wave 40 on Hard difficulty.

was a research facility surrounded by snow and ice. The map was split into two different parts. The first part was a mostly empty area with a single building, a few watchtowers, multiple trees and cliffs. Multiple other buildings in the background, a few containers and a portal to other dimensions, which had a deactivated Artificial God Cube next to it. The second part of the map was the facility itself, which was surrounded by high grey walls, which had a few towers in it. This area had three main entrances, blocked off by green barriers. Multiple watch towers, containers and lamps were in the facility.

The path started at the portal and ended at a gate inside the facility. Initially, the map started out with one path, though on Wave 2 and there on afterwards, the other two paths would be used. As the waves progressed,

would appear on paths and advance, which acted as the path's new entrance for enemies to spawn. These would make two stops until reaching the barriers. If the barriers were destroyed early, the Siege Engines would move there immediately. Barriers themselves have 100 health. When
were moving, they would kill any enemy in the way, dealing an indefinite amount of damage, instantly killing the enemy.
As the waves progressed, certain areas of the map would be bombarded. When a wave had a bombardment, an alert sound would play and the alert "

" would appear in a red box above the middle screen, the area of bombardment would also flash red a few times, notifying the players to sell their towers in the area; not doing so caused the tower to be frozen permanently and uncounted towards the placement limit.

During a bombardment, no new towers could be placed in the area and towers sold would return 100% of their cost. Locations and waves on which areas were bombarded depend on the difficulty. Some areas despite being visibly bombarded would either not affect towers in it or still allow them to be placed, due to issues with hitboxes of the bombardment.

Even though it is possible to place towers at the beginning of the map, this is generally not recommended since you will be forced to sell these towers eventually as the enemies will move forward with siege engines.
Additionally, multiple spots in the facility itself will be bombarded. You may want to avoid placing your towers in these areas to avoid having to move them later.
It is best to place support towers like
at the middle of the outpost, while placing high DPS towers like
are heavily recommended for this map as they both have extremely large range, and
ability to fly across the entire map.
also cannot be targeted by freezing attacks, making it especially useful here.
can be useful at giving your units immunity to freeze attacks from enemies that appear on this map.
